answer: Neighborhood-Gated Ingress. An agent’s peers must span multiple disjoint routing neighborhoods; the network verifies each edge via a random walk that crosses a river of low-trust relays, rejecting edges that terminate in the same cluster. A raven probe periodically challenges spanning edges with fresh routes. Under a gale of registration attempts, a sybil farm still needs genuine distinct-area links per identity, so each fake identity costs the attacker sustained relay presence in separate neighborhoods plus ongoing challenge responses—cost that scales linearly and cannot be shared.
